topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I stumbled upon an old photograph, the kind with crinkled edges and a sepia tint. It was a picture of us—two kids laughing under the old oak tree, our laughter captured in the very fibers of the image. I decided to share it with them, hoping it would spark a cherished memory. When I called, I could hear the hesitant tone in their voice, a mixture of kindness and something unfamiliar. They couldn't place the memory, couldn't recall the days we spent building forts and dreaming under the stars. I listened, my heart holding the weight of our shared past, and simply said, "That's okay. Maybe next time you’ll remember our tree."
